transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-11
Time: 15:00 PST (58 minutes)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Moss (Redwood SA), Marta Reyes (Orchid Data - Head of ML), Ben Cho (Orchid - Platform Eng), Lena Ito (Orchid - Security), Samir Naidu (Orchid - PM)

Summary (auto): Quick walkthrough of JSON-mode structured output, tool/function-calling, and how Redwood handles schema drift and runtime fallbacks. Customer wants to see resilience patterns (canary -> fallback), private deployment considerations, and how guardrails enforce contracts.

Topics covered: JSON-mode schemas, typed responses, fallback orchestration, tool routing (cost/latency), KV/prefix caching, private deployment notes (VPC/KMS), SOC2 artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan Park (AE): "All right team, thanks for joining. Quick intros? we'll do a short demo and then run a simulated failure/fallback flow. Aisha will drive the JSON-mode walkthrough."
[00:22] Marta Reyes: "Thanks, Jordan, hi everyone. main goal: we want structured responses for customer-facing financial reports, but need robust fallbacks if our external services are slow or change schema. also security needs to sign off — lena will speak to that."
[00:36] Ben Cho: "We currently have a homegrown lambda router that calls OpenAI for completions and then a post-processor to map fields; this is brittle. latency spikes kill our UI. curious how Redwood's batching and caching help and what changes our codebase."
[01:05] Aisha Patel (SE): "Great, that aligns. we'll show JSON-mode with a strict schema, then demo tool calling where the model returns a typed action to call an internal invoice-validator service. we'll also stimulate a failure and show the fallback path to a cheaper model + cached KV response."
[01:32] Riley Moss: "Small note: i'm going to toggle a simulated K-V cache hit mid-demo to show how costs and latency change, so you'll see token counts sink — real-world pattern."
[01:46] Samir Naidu: "Timeline: we're evaluating vendors this month, hope to pick a pilot by end of month. must have SSO and are leaning toward private deployment for PII data."

[02:10] Demo starts 
[02:10] Aisha: "Okay sharing screen, console -> Projects -> Schema Playground. here's the schema for the 'monthly_financial_summary' response: it enforces fields like total_revenue, revenue_by_region (array), anomalies (optional array of objects), and actions which is an enum for tool calls."
[02:38] Ben: "Quick question, if our downstream invoice-validator changes the JSON it returns, will the runtime auto-coerce or fail the call? we can't have silent corruption."
[02:58] Aisha: "Good question. in strict mode, Redwood will validate against the schema. if the tool returns unexpected shape, the runtime can auto-invoke a fallback handler: either (a) call a syntactic normalizer we register, (b) route to a different tool, or (c) return an explainable error to the caller. you can configure per-route policies."
[03:20] Marta: "Ok, so choose between soft-fix vs hard-fail. we prefer soft-fix for customer UX but hard-fail for audit logs."
[03:37] Aisha: "Exactly — we support both. you can set 'enforce_contract: true' to hard-fail and create a separate 'audit_only' path that logs the failed coercions to your console."

[04:10] Fault simulation setup
[04:10] Riley: "I'll flip the invoice-validator to return a malformed field mid-flow (simulate new version). watch the runtime detect schema drift and trigger the fallback to our pre-registered 'billing-legacy' tool."
[04:33] [screen click sounds]
[04:45] Aisha: "Initiating request: prompt asks for monthly summary, expectation is single JSON blob matching schema. sending now..."
[05:05] Console logs: 'request queued -> assigned to model: 'redwood-aurora-3b' -> batch formed (3 reqs) -> KV cache miss'
[05:30] Model returns an action: {"action":"call_tool","tool":"invoice-validator","params":{...}} (rendered in console) but the tool returns a changed payload so validation fails.
[05:57] System (auto): "Schema validation failed: anomalies[0].amount expected number got string '\"12,000\"'. Initiating fallback policy: route to 'billing-legacy' with normalizer"
[06:18] Ben: "That comma in the string, yeah we've seen that with some internal services. neat you detect it."
[06:35] Aisha: "Now watch fallback: runtime calls 'billing-legacy' which returns the normalized numeric amount. we then hydrate the model response with the coerced value and mark the original as 'original_tool_output' in audit logs."
[06:55] Marta: "Can we make the audit log append hash or redaction for PII?"
[07:07] Riley: "Yes. in Private deployments we support KMS-based field-level redaction before logs leave the cluster; we can append SHA256s for traceability."

[08:00] Security and compliance questions
[08:00] Lena Ito: "On encryption — at rest and in transit — we need to ensure keys never leave our control. does Redwood support customer-managed keys HSM/KMS in Private?"
[08:20] Jordan Park: "Yes, Private supports BYOK with KMS integrations; we have an on-prem package and VPC option. keys stay in your vault, Redwood talks to it over approved endpoints. we'll share the whitepaper and a checklist."
[08:42] Lena: "And logs — we need detailed audit trails for every model action, timestamps, user token, and which fallback path was taken."
[08:56] Aisha: "Console shows a per-request timeline and token-level cost breakdown. fallback events are annotated as 'route_override' with the policy id and reason; you can stream logs to your SIEM via our syslog/s3 connectors."
[09:20] Marta: "SSO? SAML? RBAC? we need developer and ops roles separated."
[09:30] Jordan: "We support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and a role-based access model. we'll provide the admin guide. You can lock model edits to 'admin' role so only sanctioned schema changes go live."

[10:05] Deep-dive into typed responses and runtime orchestration
[10:05] Aisha: "Switching to the schema editor: you can attach a typed contract to a route. the runtime will pre-compile validation checks and even optimize the kernel selection based on expected sequence length. that reduces tail latency."
[10:34] Ben: "Kernel selection? i thought that was internal — what do we get visibility into?"
[10:43] Riley: "You see a performance profile in the model catalog: expected p50/p99 under different batch sizes. For Dedicated we can lock an optimized kernel set if you need stable p99s."
[11:02] Samir: "If we run a canary and kernel-level perf depends on seq len, do you auto-select different model variants?"
[11:12] Aisha: "Yes — smart routing can pick by latency SLO, cost target, or region. you can pin a route to prefer quantized variants for cost or float models for higher fidelity."

[12:05] Simulated cascade: model slow -> routing fallback to cheaper model + cached KV
[12:05] Aisha: "Now simulate model latency spike — setting the primary model to 2s per token to force routing. watch the router route to 'redwood-aurora-1q' and serve from a KV-cached prefix response."
[12:30] Console: 'router: latency_slo_violation -> fallback plan 'BATCH_FAST' applied -> model switched -> KV cache hit -> response 320ms'
[12:50] Marta: "That's a huge difference, but how do we ensure hallucination rates don't spike when switching models?"
[13:05] Aisha: "We keep a rune: quality budget per route and tie it to evals. if the cheaper model exceeds an acceptable drift threshold, router will instead serve a cached certified response or fail closed. You can set 'quality_failover: true' to prefer cached certified outputs over lower-quality runtime variants."

[14:00] Questions from the customer
[14:00] Ben: "What does the PoC look like? can we test with our real traffic or only synthetic data?"
[14:13] Jordan: "We usually start with a shadow PoC: mirror a subset of traffic into a dedicated sandbox so no customer-visible effect, that gives realistic signals without risk."
[14:25] Marta: "Data residency — we need all EU traffic to stay in eu-west. is routing by region supported?"
[14:35] Riley: "Yes, region-aware routing; you can pin routes to region or set a policy: prefer eu-west then us-west as fallback."

[15:00] Pricing & capacity
[15:00] Jordan: "Discussing numbers quickly — hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved capacity. for a low-latency front-end we'd recommend Dedicated with burst capacity for peaks. i'll send a draft pricing sheet after this call."
[15:25] Samir: "Budget constraint: we'd prefer not to exceed a soft cap; is there programmatic throttling?"
[15:33] Aisha: "Yes, you can set token budgets per route and programmatic throttles; Console enforces quotas and emits alerts."

[16:10] Technical question about tool auth and signatures
[16:10] Ben: "When Redwood calls our internal tools (invoice-validator), what auth flows are supported? We don't want Redis or internal services exposed publicly."
[16:22] Riley: "We support outbound VPC peering and service accounts with short-lived tokens. For private deployments, the runtime sits inside your VPC so calls are internal; we also support mTLS to service endpoints."
[16:43] Ben: "And can we require signed tool responses?"
[16:48] Aisha: "Yes, you can require tool responses to include an HMAC signature we verify before ingest. that becomes part of the validation pipeline."

[18:00] Edge cases and regret analysis
[18:00] Marta: "If fallback normalized values differ materially, how do we do regression/eval?"
[18:10] Aisha: "We log both original and normalized outputs and tie them to eval sets. Optimize runs continuous regression tests on your prompt set and flags quality deltas per model or per tool path."
[18:32] Riley: "We also emit a 'drift' metric you can hook into alerts and trigger a canary rollback."

[20:00] Live Q&A and some stuttering, cross talk
[20:00] Samir: "So to confirm: we can enforce schema, have fallback tool routing, and audit all steps?"
[20:08] Aisha: "Yes. and the console shows the per-request timeline: model call, tool calls, validation, fallback events, final assembly, and token costs."
[20:18] [crosstalk] Marta: "And if we want to ship a hotfix to the schema, how do we avoid breaking production?"
[20:24] Jordan: "We recommend staged rollouts: you can do canary with 5% traffic, ramp to 25%, etc. There's also an automated 'schema-migrate' preview which runs the new schema against a sample corpus and surfaces errors before activation."

[22:00] Operational notes
[22:00] Aisha: "For the PoC, we'll propose: mirror 3k daily requests into a sandbox for two weeks, run fallback simulation and drift evals, and provide a dashboard with token/cost breakdowns. After that, you can opt into Dedicated if SLOs require it."
[22:25] Ben: "Do you have sample SLO templates?"
[22:30] Jordan: "Yes — will include SLO examples and a recommended SLA for Dedicated customers."

[25:00] Final recap and next steps
[25:00] Jordan: "Recap: Redwood will share pricing + SOW, the SE team will provision a sandbox and run a fallback sim, customer will provide corpus/schema, security will get the KMS checklist. we'll target PoC kickoff 2027-11-17."
[25:30] Marta: "Sounds good. Lena will review KMS checklist and confirm redactions. Ben will coordinate mirror traffic. I'll get the prompt corpus together."
[25:48] Jordan: "I'll follow up with calendar invite and link to the private docs repo. Also attaching the 'JSON-mode best practices' link: https://redwood.ai/docs/json-mode and our 'Private deployment whitepaper' at https://redwood.ai/whitepapers/private-deploy"

[26:10] Closing chatter
[26:10] Samir: "Thanks, this was useful. quick note — any benchmarks vs Anthropic on latency?"
[26:18] Riley: "We have perf sheets; i'll include a p50/p99 comparison in the packet — data varies by model and seq length but we'll give normalized numbers."
[26:32] Marta: "Ok thanks everyone."
[26:35] Jordan: "Thanks all, we'll follow up. meeting end."

Note: transcript has small transcription artifacts: punctuation and some product names may be slightly off (e.g., 'K-V cache' vs KV cache), filler words preserved.
